To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BIA and ADP are valid measures of body composition and the US is a valid measure of total abdominal fat, but not visceral fat.
the octopolar bioelectrical impedance, ultrasound and air displacement plethysmography are all reliable measures of body composition.
the octopolar bioelectrical impedance (BIA) and the ultrasound (US) are valid and reliable tools for assessing body composition and abdominal fat depths.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the validation of three clinical-grade measures (BIA, ADP and US) of body composition and a comparison of the US scans to the octopolar Bioimpedance BIA.
the validation and comparison of three body composition techniques, with a focus on the comparison of ultrasound abdominal fat depths against an octopolar B.I.A device.
the validation of three body composition techniques and comparing ultrasound fat depths to an octopolar bioelectrical impedance device.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the US abdominal fat depths can be a valid measure of body fat, but only when compared to a trunk fat %BF from a BIA.
all three clinical-grade body composition machines are valid and reliable for measuring body composition and that the US is a valid method for measuring visceral and subcutaneous abdominal fat.
the US is a valid tool for assessing total abdominal, sub cutaneous and visceral fat depth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BIA is a valid and cost effective way to measure total body fat and visceral fat in the trunk region.

all three clinical-grade body composition machines were validated against one another and that the US scans of the total abdominal, sub cutaneous and visceral fat depth were not significantly correlated to the BIA trunk fat %BF, but were significantly different from each other.
the BIA and ADP are valid measures of body composition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the US is not a valid measure of visceral fat, while it is valid for subcutaneous and total abdominal fat depths.
the US and the BIA can be used interchangeably in clinical and field settings, while the ADP should be reserved for use in the lab setting.
all three devices used in our study were significantly correlated with each other.
